newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel's Elite sells European plants.
newsitem.headline: Israel's Elite sells European plants.

text.p: Israel's Elite Industries Ltd said it would receive 18.3 million German marks for two coffee-manufacturing plants plants in Spain and France that it has agreed to sell to the Dutch food company Drie Mollen BV.

Drie Mollen will also pay 0.8-1.8 million marks for equipment and pay royalties for the use of a number of coffee brand names over the next five years, Elite said on Monday. At the end of the period, the brand names will be transferred to Drie Mollen, closely held company.
Elite, Israel's largest food company, said it would take an 11.3 million shekel loss on the sale, most of it in the fourth quarter. The sale is expected to be completed December 17.

The sale comes as Elite seeks to pare back its loss-making Western European operations, which it acquired in 1992. The company closed its Berlin coffee-making plant and other unprofitable production lines earlier this year.
As a result, overseas sales fell 30.6 percent in the first nine months to 674.3 million shekels, or 44 percent of the company's total.

Elite still has a Belgian coffee plant, which may still be sold, as well as a confectionery business in France. Elite, which is Israel's leading maker of coffee and confectioneries, has been much more successful in eastern Europe, with distribution and manufacturing operations in Poland and Romania.
The company has eight production plants making private-label coffee and confectioneries in six countries.
